{"rules": ["Model consistently underestimates the magnitude of upward price spikes (e.g., Example 1 & 2) by failing to fully incorporate the momentum from recent high sentiment days.", "Forecast trajectory is overly smooth and linear, ignoring the high volatility and mean-reverting behavior seen in true outcomes after initial rallies.", "Sentiment history shows a lagged effect; positive sentiment peaks precede price spikes, but the model fails to amplify this signal into a steeper upward slope.", "Model exhibits a 'floor' bias where it caps upside potential even when recent history (last 3-5 days) shows strong uptrends and neutral-to-positive sentiment.", "Correction heuristic: Apply a volatility multiplier to the forecast during periods of rising sentiment, specifically increasing the projected rate of change by 10-15% above the model's baseline slope.", "When sentiment is positive or neutral while price history shows a sustained increase (e.g., >2% daily gain), override the model's conservative projection with a more aggressive upward trend.", "Account for 'spike decay' in true outcomes; if the model predicts a steady climb, adjust the forecast to include sharper peaks followed by immediate mean reversion corrections.", "Reduce forecast confidence during high-sentiment windows as the model systematically misses the peak of rallies, suggesting a need for higher variance bands."]
}
